content.title: Jamie’s St. Patrick’s Weekend WX Forecast for March 13, 2026
content.text: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WTOC) - Let the parades begin! Tybee and Hilton Head will hold their St. Patrick’s Day parades this weekend and both weekend days will be warm, but one will have some spotty downpours. Big changes on Monday with the possibility of severe weather from a widely impactful cold front; it’s a First Alert Weather Day.High pressure will be in total control Saturday with wall-to-wall sunshine. Patchy fog possible in the morning, 49°, high 80°. High at the beaches will be 70° when the Tybee Island Irish Heritage Parade begins at 3pm.Sunday spotty showers will develop from the south and along the coast and move south to north through the morning and early afternoon. 58/80, 40% chance of rain. Low 70s for the beginning of the Hilton Head Island St. Patrick’s Day Parade and a spotty shower will be lurking most likely before the parade at 2pm, but be wet weather ready.Monday is a First Alert Weather Day: A strong cold front will bring rain and gusty winds and the possibility of severe thunderstorms. The main concern is damaging wind gusts; however isolated tornadoes are possible. Even outside of a severe storm, we will be windy with 30-35mph wind gusts and warm with a morning low of 66 and an afternoon high of 76.THEN! A frost/freeze is possible Monday night and Tuesday night in the wake of the cold front. On Monday if you live west of I-95, you could have some frost. Tuesday the frost/freeze will be more widespread generally for all of us away from the beaches.Tuesday, Saint Patrick’s Day: 34/53 sunny and breezy - NW 15mph with gusts 20-25mph.Wednesday: 33/61 mostly sunny. There could be some upper 20s in the morning along GA Hwy 301, US 1, Hwy 84.Thursday: 40/69 mostly sunnyFriday: 45/76 mostly sunnyMARINE: NE winds 5 kt, becoming SE late this evening, then becoming W late, seas 3 to 4 ft. Saturday...N winds 5 kt, becoming E in the afternoon, seas 2 to 3 ft. Saturday night...seas 2 to 3 ft, seas 2 to 3 ft. Saturday night...E winds 5 to 10 kt, seas 2 to 3 ft. Sunday...E winds 10 kt, seas 2 to 3 ft, showers likely, possible thunderstorm. Sunday night...SE winds 10 to 15 kt, becoming S 15 to 20 kt, seas 3 to 4 ft building to 5-6 ft after midnight, chance of storms. Monday...S winds 20 to 25 kt, becoming SW 25 to 30 kt in the afternoon, seas 5 to 7 ft, building to 6 to 8 ft in the afternoon.Stay Safe!~JErtleCopyright 2026 WTOC. All rights reserved.
